mainTopic: Whether a קנס of the Sages passes to the sinner's son, and the laws of a slave sold to a buyer outside ארץ ישראל.
overview: The גמרא first asks whether a קנס of the Sages falls on the person who sinned or on his property. The answer matters because it decides whether his son must pay after he dies. Two traditions show that the penalty is on the person, not his son: a field fertilized in שביעית, and someone who made his friend's טהרות impure. Next, a ברייתא teaches that a slave sold to a buyer outside ארץ ישראל goes free, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that this depends on where the buyer really lives. רבי ירמיה asks about slaves a wife brings into a marriage with a man from בבל who plans to go back, and the question ends in תיקו. רבי יוחנן rules that a slave sold in סוריא goes free only if his master had planned to return. Finally, רב ענן recalls two rulings of שמואל but cannot remember which one returns the buyer's money. רב יוסף works it out: in the slave case the money is not returned, and in the field sold during יובל it is.

steps.title: Is the penalty on the person or on his property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא makes the earlier question sharper. Even if the son is not penalized when his father planned work for חול המועד, maybe this case is different, because here the Sages may have penalized the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if you say that when a man planned his work for חול המועד and then died, his son is not penalized, because the son did nothing wrong, what is the law here? Did the Sages penalize the man himself, and he is gone? Or did they penalize his property, and the property is still here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking a clear either/or question about who the Sages' penalty is aimed at: the person, or his money and belongings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the חול המועד case the penalty is plainly on the person who planned the work, so it ends when he dies. In our case it is possible that the Sages aimed the penalty at the property itself. If so, the property is still here and the son would have to pay. The whole question depends on what the target of the קנס is.

keyTerms.meaning: And even if you decide (one side of the question), there is still a further question
He planned his work so that it would fall on חול המועד
A penalty / they penalized (a fine set by the Sages)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חול המועד case is the main topic. It is only used as a comparison to make the main question (the man who sold his slave and then died) sharper.

phrases.english: And if you say:
phrases.notes: This means: even if we already decided the first point, there is still another question.

phrases.english: "He planned his work for the festival's middle days,
and he died, they did not penalize his son after him"
because he did not do a forbidden act,
phrases.notes: "He" here is the son. The son himself did nothing wrong.

phrases.english: here, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "Here" is the case being asked about: a man who sold his slave to a non-Jew and then died.

phrases.english: Did the Sages penalize him personally,
and he is no longer here;
or perhaps the Sages penalized his property,
and it is still here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question from before this section (selling a slave to a non-Jew and then dying) and makes it sharper.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a קנס דרבנן aimed at the person, so it ends when he dies, or at his property, so it continues against his heirs?

steps.title: A source from the laws of the seventh year
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers that the question can be settled from the laws of שביעית. A field that was only cleared of thorns may be sown after שביעית. A field that was fertilized may not be sown, as a penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it. A field that was cleared of thorns during שביעית may be sown after שביעית ends. If it was improved with fertilizer, or animals were kept on it to fertilize it, it may not be sown after שביעית ends.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source about a penalty in שביעית. This is the setup for the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clearing thorns is a minor act, so there is no penalty. Fertilizing the field is real forbidden work, so the Sages penalized the owner by not letting him sow it after שביעית. This gives us a clear example of a קנס, and the next step will ask whom this קנס falls on.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a source)
After the seventh year has ended
Animals were penned on it so their manure would fertilize it

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
A field that was cleared of thorns in the seventh year,
may be sown after the seventh year ends.
If it was improved or had animals penned on it,
it may not be sown after the seventh year ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question by bringing a source that contains a penalty.
steps.raayaObject: Whom a קנס דרבנן falls on
steps.raayaSupportSource: The laws of a field worked on in שביעית

steps.title: The son may sow the field, so the penalty is on the person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא has a tradition that if the father fertilized the field and died, his son may sow it. So the Sages penalize the sinner himself, not his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: We have a tradition that if he fertilized the field and then died, his son may sow it. This shows that the Sages penalized the man himself, and they did not penalize his son.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the proof is completed. The penalty on the fertilized field disappears once the father dies, so the penalty must have been on him personally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field, which is the property, is still here, yet the son may sow it. That means the קנס was never on the property; it was on the person. This answers the question: the son of the man who sold his slave would also not be penalized.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule: a קנס דרבנן falls on the sinner himself (לדידיה), not on his son after him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle settles the main question: when the father dies, the penalty does not pass to his heirs.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, נָקְטִינַן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said: We have a tradition:
If he improved it and died, his son may sow it.
This shows that the Sages penalized him personally,
they did not penalize his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the שביעית source from step 2 to answer the question from step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Sages penalize the person himself, so the son is not penalized after him.

steps.title: אביי: the son does not pay for impure טהרות
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition: if someone made his friend's pure items impure and then died, his son does not have to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that if someone made his friend's pure items impure and then died, the Sages did not penalize his son after him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings another case that follows the same rule, that the penalty does not pass to the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making someone's טהרות impure causes him a real loss, but the obligation to pay comes from the Sages. When the one who did it dies, his son does not have to pay. This fits the rule from step 3.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition:
If he made his friend's pure items impure, and died,
the Sages did not penalize his son after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case that fits the same principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If someone made another person's טהרות impure and then died, his son does not pay.

steps.title: Why: hidden damage is only a penalty from the Sages
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that damage you cannot see is not damage by Torah law. The payment is only a קנס from the Sages, and such a קנס falls on the person, not his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Damage that cannot be seen is not considered damage, and the payment is a penalty from the Sages. The Sages penalized him personally; they did not penalize his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי's case works this way: the payment is only a קנס דרבנן, so the rule from before applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing visibly changed in the items, so by Torah law it is not damage and there is no Torah debt to pay. The obligation comes only from the Sages, and the Sages' penalties end with the person who did the act.

keyTerms.meaning: A penalty made by the Sages

steps.confusionAlert: The son is not exempt because the damage was not real. He is exempt because the payment is only a קנס from the Sages, and such a קנס falls only on the one who did the act.
steps.whatToRemember: Two cases, the fertilized field in שביעית and the impure טהרות, both show the same rule: a קנס דרבנן falls on the sinner and not on his son.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: הֶיזֵּק שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר לָא שְׁמֵיהּ הֶיזֵּק,
phrases.english: Damage that cannot be seen is not called damage,
and it is a penalty of the Sages,
the Sages penalized him personally,
they did not penalize his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind אביי's ruling in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Damage that cannot be seen is only a קנס דרבנן, and a קנס falls on the person, not his son.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Payment for damage that cannot be seen is a קנס דרבנן, so it does not pass to the heirs.

steps.title: A slave sold to someone outside the land goes free
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'or outside the land' and brings a ברייתא: a slave sold to a Jew outside ארץ ישראל goes free, but still needs a גט שחרור from his second master.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Or outside the land': The Rabbis taught: if someone sells his slave to a buyer outside ארץ ישראל, the slave goes free, but he still needs a document of freedom from his second master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the slave was sold to someone outside ארץ ישראל, he goes free. Even so, he formally still needs a גט שחרור, and it comes from the new owner, the buyer. Step 24 learns from this that the sale really took effect.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes out to freedom; the slave is freed
A document that frees a slave

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the first master writes the גט שחרור. The ברייתא says it comes from the second master, the one who bought him.

phrases.english: 'Or to outside the land':
phrases.notes: These are words from our משנה: one who sells his slave to a non-Jew or to someone outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who sells his slave to outside the land –
he goes out to freedom,
but he needs a document of freedom from his second master.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמּוֹכֵר עַבְדּוֹ לְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a new clause of the משנה, separate from the discussion of penalties on heirs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave sold to a buyer outside ארץ ישראל goes free, but still needs a גט שחרור from the buyer.

steps.title: It depends on how the buyer is described
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the slave sometimes goes free and sometimes not. If the seller said he sold him to 'so-and-so from אנטוכיא,' the slave does not go free. If he said 'from אנטוכיא who lives in אנטוכיא,' the slave goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: sometimes he goes free and sometimes he does not. How so? If the master said, 'My slave so-and-so, I sold him to so-and-so the man from אנטוכיא,' he does not go free. If he said, 'to the man from אנטוכיא who is in אנטוכיא,' he goes free.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a condition to the ruling: the slave only goes free if we know for sure the buyer lives outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling someone 'from אנטוכיא' may only mean he comes from there, while he may live in ארץ ישראל now. So the slave stays a slave. Only when the seller clearly says the buyer lives in אנטוכיא do we know the slave is leaving the land.

keyTerms.meaning: A man from אנטוכיא, a city outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Sometimes he goes free, and sometimes he does not go free.
How so?
If he said: 'So-and-so my slave,
I sold him to so-and-so the man from Antioch' –
he does not go free.
'To the man from Antioch who is in Antioch' – he goes free.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: פְּעָמִים יָצָא, וּפְעָמִים לֹא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the first ruling: the slave goes free only when it is clear the buyer lives outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Sold to a man from אנטוכיא' does not free the slave; 'sold to a man from אנטוכיא who is in אנטוכיא' does.

steps.title: A ruling that seems to say the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a teaching that 'I sold him to a man from אנטוכיא' does free the slave, and only 'a man from אנטוכיא who lives in לוד' does not. This seems to contradict רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught: 'I sold him to a man from אנטוכיא' – he goes free. 'To a man from אנטוכיא who lives in לוד' – he does not go free!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבן שמעון בן גמליאל with a ruling that treats the plain words 'man from אנטוכיא' the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said plain 'man from אנטוכיא' does not free the slave. This ruling says those same words do free him, unless the seller adds that the buyer lives in לוד. The same words get opposite results.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is taught (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
לוד, a city inside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
'I sold him to a man from Antioch' – he goes free,
'To a man from Antioch who lives in Lod' – he does not go free!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 7 with a ruling that seems to contradict it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling that 'sold to a man from אנטוכיא' does not free the slave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ruling says those exact words do free the slave, so the two rulings contradict each other.

steps.title: House versus inn in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two rulings speak about different buyers. If the man from אנטוכיא owns a house in ארץ ישראל, the slave does not go free. If he only stays at an inn there, the slave goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling is when he has a house in ארץ ישראל, and that ruling is when he has only an inn in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each ruling is about a different kind of buyer from אנטוכיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer who owns a house in ארץ ישראל may have bought the slave to serve there, so he does not go free (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's case). A buyer who only has an inn here really lives abroad, so the slave goes free (the other ruling's case).

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources can both be right
An inn, a temporary place to stay

steps.whatToRemember: A slave sold to a buyer from abroad goes free only if the buyer's real home is outside ארץ ישראל. Owning a house here means the slave may stay here. Staying at an inn here does not.

phrases.english: It is not difficult,

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ בֵּיתָא בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: this is where he has a house in Eretz Yisrael,
phrases.notes: This is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's case, where the slave does not go free.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ אוּשְׁפִּיזָא בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: that is where he has an inn in Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ בֵּיתָא בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different kind of buyer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings were about the same buyer from אנטוכיא, so they clashed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Owns a house in ארץ ישראל: the slave does not go free. Only stays at an inn: the slave goes free.

steps.title: Slaves a wife brings to a husband from בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks: a man from בבל married a woman in ארץ ישראל, she brought slaves into the marriage, and he plans to go back to בבל. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: a man from בבל married a woman in ארץ ישראל, and she brought him male and female slaves, and he plans to go back. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a new question that builds on the rule about slaves taken out of ארץ ישראל. The גמרא is setting up a discussion that will continue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here nobody sold the slaves; they came to the husband through the marriage. The question is whether this counts like a sale to someone who will take them out of the land, so they would go free.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; he raised a question
And she brought into the marriage for him
And he plans to go back

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן בָּבֶל שֶׁנָּשָׂא אִשָּׁה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: A man from Babylonia who married a woman in Eretz Yisrael,
and she brought him male and female slaves,
and he plans to go back, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means going back to בבל, which would take the slaves out of ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule about slaves leaving ארץ ישראל and asks if it applies when slaves come through a marriage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does bringing slaves into a marriage with a man who plans to leave ארץ ישראל count like selling them abroad, so that they go free?

steps.title: The question works under both opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי ירמיה's question applies both to the view that 'the law is with her' and to the view that 'the law is with him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The question can be asked according to the one who says 'the law is with her,' and also according to the one who says 'the law is with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It announces that רבי ירמיה's question is a real question under both sides of an earlier argument, and it will explain each side next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an earlier argument about whose claim to a wife's slaves is stronger, hers or her husband's. You might think that argument settles רבי ירמיה's question. The גמרא says no: the question stays open whichever side you follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be asked. The question applies here.
According to the one who says
The law is with her. Her claim to the slaves is stronger.
The law is with him. His claim to the slaves is stronger.

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to the one who says 'the law is with her,'
phrases.notes: This refers to an earlier argument about who keeps the wife's slaves if the couple divorces.

phrases.english: let it be asked according to the one who says 'the law is with him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places רבי ירמיה's question from Step 10 inside an earlier argument and says it applies under both sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי ירמיה's question depend on the argument over whether the law is with her or with him?

steps.title: The question under the view that the law is with her
steps.stepSummary: Under 'the law is with her,' the slaves might count as hers, so moving them abroad is not like a sale. Or they might count as his, because he is owed the profits from their work.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says 'the law is with her': since the law is with her, maybe the slaves are treated as hers. Or maybe, since the slaves are tied to him for their profits, they are treated as his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is still open even if her claim is stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: her claim is stronger, so the slaves are hers. The husband taking them to בבל would not count as a buyer taking them abroad. Side two: the husband is owed the profits of their work, and that tie may be enough to treat them as his, as if he had bought them.

keyTerms.meaning: They are tied to someone, owed to them
Profits. Here, the gain from the slaves' work.

phrases.english: Let it be asked according to the one who says 'the law is with her':
since the law is with her, they are treated as hers;
phrases.notes: Watch the spelling: כדידה means 'hers' and כדידיה means 'his.' The question turns on that difference.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא, כֵּיוָן דִּמְשַׁעְבְּדִי לֵיהּ לְפֵירָא,
phrases.english: or perhaps, since they are tied to him for the profits,
they are treated as his?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the first half of Step 11's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Even if her claim is stronger, does his right to the profits make the slaves count as his?

steps.title: The question under the view that the law is with him
steps.stepSummary: Under 'the law is with him,' the slaves might count as his. Or they might count as hers, because he never owned the slaves themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says 'the law is with him': since the law is with him, maybe the slaves are treated as his. Or maybe, since he did not acquire the slave's body, they are treated as hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is still open even if his claim is stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: his claim is stronger, so the slaves are his, and taking them abroad is like a buyer taking them out. Side two: he only owns the right to their work, not the slaves themselves, so they may still count as hers.

keyTerms.meaning: Its body. Here, the slave himself, as opposed to his work.

phrases.english: And let it be asked according to the one who says 'the law is with him':
since the law is with him, they are treated as his;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא קָנֵי לֵיהּ לְגוּפֵיהּ –
phrases.english: or perhaps, since he did not acquire the slave's body itself,
they are treated as hers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the second half of Step 11's claim, mirroring Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Even if his claim is stronger, does his lack of ownership of the slaves themselves make them count as hers?

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבי ירמיה's question with תיקו. No answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבי ירמיה's question without deciding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under both opinions there was a good reason to treat the slaves as his and a good reason to treat them as hers. Since neither side could be proven, the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question is left without an answer.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה's question about the wife's slaves stays open under both opinions. Do the slaves count as hers (ownership) or as his (rights to their work)? Neither side wins.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question laid out in Steps 10-13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question is unresolved: it is unclear whether the wife's slaves count as hers or her husband's.

steps.title: A slave sold by his master in סוריא goes free
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports that רבי יוחנן taught him: a slave who followed his master to סוריא, and was sold there by his master, goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: רבי יוחנן taught me: a slave who went out after his master to סוריא, and his master sold him there, goes out to freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. A slave sold in סוריא is treated like a slave sold outside ארץ ישראל, so he goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail is that the slave left ארץ ישראל on his own, following his master. Even so, רבי יוחנן says the sale in סוריא sets him free.

keyTerms.meaning: סוריא (Syria), a land outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, שָׁנָה לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: Rabbi Yoḥanan taught me:
a slave who went out after his master to Syria,
and his master sold him there,
goes out to freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, שָׁנָה לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about selling a slave outside ארץ ישראל, building on Step 6's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave who followed his master to סוריא and was sold there goes free.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי חייא: the slave lost his right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from רבי חייא's teaching that such a slave lost his right to go free.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חייא taught: he lost his right!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling it just quoted from רבי יוחנן, using a teaching of רבי חייא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the slave goes free. רבי חייא says the slave lost his right to freedom. These seem to clash directly, so the גמרא will need to explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught. This opens a challenge.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya teach:
he lost his right!
phrases.notes: He means the slave lost his right to go free, because he chose to leave ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the slave sold in סוריא goes free.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא taught that this same slave lost his right to freedom. The two teachings contradict each other.

steps.title: It depends on whether the master planned to return
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי חייא are talking about two different cases. If the master planned to return, the slave goes free. If not, he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. One ruling is where the master planned to return. The other is where the master did not plan to return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between רבי יוחנן and רבי חייא by splitting them into two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the master meant to come back, the slave left ארץ ישראל only for a short trip. So selling him in סוריא is like selling him out of the land, and he goes free (רבי יוחנן). If the master left for good and the slave chose to go with him, the slave gave up that right (רבי חייא).

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really clash
Here... there; each source is about a different case
His master's plan to come back to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: It is not difficult.
Here, where his master's intention is to return,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's case, where the slave goes free.

phrases.english: there, where his master does not intend to return.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן שֶׁדַּעַת רַבּוֹ לַחְזוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from רבי חייא in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן and רבי חייא disagree about the same slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each is talking about a different case, depending on the master's plan to return.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this split
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to teach this same split, starting with the words 'the slave goes out after his master to סוריא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it is taught in a ברייתא: The slave goes out after his master to סוריא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that supports the answer it just gave. This sets up the next step, where the wording gets questioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא (fully quoted in step 20) uses the very same split: did the master plan to return or not. But its opening word 'goes out' sounds like a rule that the slave must go, which causes a problem right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Syria, an area outside ארץ ישראל with an in-between status

phrases.english: And so it is taught in a ברייתא:
The slave goes out after his master to סוריא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: יוֹצֵא הָעֶבֶד אַחַר רַבּוֹ לְסוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The split between a master who plans to return and one who does not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a slave who goes with his master to סוריא.

steps.title: Must the slave go along?
steps.stepSummary: The word 'goes out' sounds like the slave has to follow his master. But a משנה teaches that nobody can be forced to leave ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Goes out'?! Can he not refuse to go?! But we learned in a משנה: Not everyone can make others leave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the ברייתא. It sounds like the slave is required to go, which can't be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in כתובות teaches that a master cannot force his slave to leave ארץ ישראל. So the ברייתא cannot mean the slave must follow. Its wording needs to be read differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Not everyone can force others to leave ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: "Goes out"?!
Is it impossible for him not to go out?!
But we learned in a משנה:
And not everyone can take others out!
phrases.notes: From the משנה in כתובות 110b: a master can't force his slave to leave ארץ ישראל with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word יוֹצֵא in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Present tense 'goes out' sounds like a duty, but a משנה says a slave cannot be forced to leave ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Read it as 'went out', after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really means: if a slave already went with his master to סוריא and was sold there, then whether the master is forced to free him depends on whether he planned to return.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: if a slave went with his master to סוריא, and his master sold him there: if the master planned to return, we force him to free the slave. If the master did not plan to return, we do not force him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading. The ברייתא is not saying the slave must go. It describes what happens after he already went.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing יוֹצֵא ('goes out') to יָצָא ('went out') removes the problem from the משנה. The rest of the ברייתא shows the exact split from step 17, so the support holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; a fix to how the text is read
We force him (the master) to free the slave

steps.whatToRemember: A slave sold in סוריא goes free only if his master had planned to return to ארץ ישראל. If the master left for good and the slave chose to go with him, the slave has no claim.

phrases.english: Rather, read it this way:
If the slave went out after his master to סוריא,
and his master sold him there:
if his master intended to return,
we force him,
phrases.notes: Him means the master. He is forced to set the slave free.

phrases.english: and if his master did not intend to return,
we do not force him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יָצָא הָעֶבֶד אַחַר רַבּוֹ לְסוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 19 and completes the support from step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says a slave must follow his master.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא describes a slave who already chose to go, and the ruling depends on the master's plan to return.

steps.title: רב ענן heard two rulings from שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן says he heard two rulings from שמואל. One is this slave ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: I heard two things from מר שמואל. One is this one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן says the slave ruling was one of two teachings he heard from שמואל. This sets up the second one, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first teaching is the basic rule that a slave sold to a buyer outside ארץ ישראל goes free. That is the rule רב יוסף uses in step 24, not the סוריא ruling of רבי יוחנן. רב ענן then brings in a second, unrelated ruling that he remembers together with the first.

phrases.english: רב ענן said:
I heard two things from מר שמואל:
one is this one;
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a slave sold to someone outside ארץ ישראל goes free.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן, שְׁמַעִית מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the rule about a slave sold outside ארץ ישראל to שמואל and opens a second teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The slave ruling is one of two teachings רב ענן heard from שמואל.

steps.title: Selling a field in the יובל year itself
steps.stepSummary: The second ruling is about someone who sells his field during the יובל year itself. רב says the sale works, but the field goes right back. שמואל says the sale does not work at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one is what was stated: if someone sells his field in the יובל year itself, רב said: it is sold, and it goes out. שמואל said: it is not sold at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second ruling רב ענן heard from שמואל: a dispute between רב and שמואל about selling a field in the יובל year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fields sold earlier go back to their owner in יובל. Here the sale happens during יובל itself. רב says the sale takes effect but the field leaves the buyer right away. שמואל says no sale happens at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The יובל (Jubilee) year, when sold fields return to their owners
It is sold, and it goes back out

phrases.english: and the other is what was stated:
One who sells his field in the יובל year itself:
רב said: it is sold, and it goes out.
phrases.notes: Goes out means it leaves the buyer and returns to the seller right away.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: And שמואל said: it is not sold at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ – דְּאִיתְּמַר: הַמּוֹכֵר שָׂדֵהוּ בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the two rulings רב ענן announced in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling a field during יובל: רב says it is sold but goes right back; שמואל says it is not sold at all.

steps.title: רב ענן forgets which case returns the money
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן says that in one of שמואל's two rulings the sale money goes back to the buyer, and in the other it does not. He does not remember which is which.
steps.simpleTranslation: In one case the money of the sale goes back, and in the other case it does not go back. But I don't know which one is which.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן finishes his report of שמואל's two rulings by admitting a gap in his memory. This sets up the next move, where someone tries to figure out the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rulings are about a sale that does not fully stand: the slave sold to outside ארץ ישראל, and the field sold during יובל. רב ענן remembers that only one of them gives the buyer a refund. He no longer knows whether the refund belongs to the slave case or the field case.

keyTerms.meaning: The sale money goes back (to the buyer)

phrases.english: In one, the sale money goes back,
and in one, the sale money does not go back;
and I do not know which of them is which.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב ענן's report of שמואל's two rulings and adds a doubt about the refund in each case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In which of שמואל's two cases does the buyer get his money back: the slave sold outside ארץ ישראל, or the field sold during יובל?

steps.title: Proof that in the slave case the money is not returned
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא. A slave sold to outside ארץ ישראל goes free, but he needs a גט שחרור from his second master. This shows the second master really bought him, so the buyer does not get his money back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Let's work it out. A ברייתא teaches that if someone sells his slave to outside ארץ ישראל, the slave goes free, but he still needs a document of freedom from his second master. So we learn that the second master really acquired him, and the money does not go back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא to solve רב ענן's doubt for the slave case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slave needs a גט שחרור from the second master. Only an owner can write a document of freedom, so the second master's purchase must have worked. If the sale worked, there is no reason to cancel it and refund the money, so the buyer loses his money when he has to free the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see for ourselves (let's work it out)
A document that frees a slave
Learn from it (a proof is being drawn)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the slave law is a penalty that does not cancel the sale. The sale works and the buyer must free the slave at his own loss.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Let us see for ourselves,
from what is taught in a baraita:
One who sells his slave to outside the Land
he goes out to freedom,
but he needs a document of freedom from his second master.
Learn from this: his second master acquired him,
and the sale money does not go back;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: נִיחְזֵי אֲנַן, מִדְּתָנֵי בְּבָרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ענן's doubt by proving which ruling belongs to the slave case.
steps.raayaObject: That in the slave case the buyer does not get his money back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying the slave sold outside ארץ ישראל needs a גט שחרור from his second master. That shows the sale worked.

steps.title: So in the field case the money is returned
steps.stepSummary: Since the slave case does not give a refund, the case with the refund must be the field. When שמואל said a field sold during יובל "is not sold," he meant the sale is void and the money goes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so, when שמואל said there that the field is not sold, the money goes back to the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף finishes his proof by assigning the other ruling to the field case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ענן remembered that exactly one case gives a refund. The slave case does not, so the field case does. Here "not sold" means the sale never took effect, so the buyer gets his money back.
steps.whatToRemember: Slave sold to outside ארץ ישראל: the sale works, he must be freed, and the buyer loses his money. Field sold during יובל (according to שמואל): the sale is void and the money goes back.

phrases.english: And when Shmuel said there
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of selling a field during the יובל year itself, from step 22.

phrases.english: "it is not sold" —
the money goes back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָתָם אֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the other half of the answer from the proof in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In שמואל's ruling on a field sold during יובל, the sale is void and the buyer gets his money back. In the slave case, the buyer does not.
